data.title: Semantic HTML
data.tagline: HTML tags that mark each section's role in the document, such as headings, lists, and navigation
data.learningOutcome: You can check whether heading tags reflect the page content hierarchy, including whether multiple H1s make sense.
data.description: When structuring a web page, semantic HTML tags mark content roles, such as headings for sections, nav for navigation, and ul for lists. Screen readers can navigate by headings; font size is visual styling, not structure. HTML allows multiple H1 elements on a page. Heading levels should reflect the content hierarchy so the outline is easy to follow.

learning.assumes: You have seen page outlines or SEO check messages, or heard of heading levels.
learning.outcome: You can check whether heading tags reflect the page content hierarchy, including whether multiple H1s make sense.

distinctions.label: Visual hierarchy
distinctions.explanation: Visual hierarchy expresses importance through font size and only looks big; heading levels mark structure with tags and are machine-readable.

distinctions.label: Page title tag
distinctions.explanation: The page title only sets the text shown on the browser tab; the H1 is the main heading in the page body—different positions.

explanation.title: Use H1 according to the content
explanation.text: HTML allows multiple H1s; check whether each marks a distinct main section instead of deleting one just because of the count.

explanation.title: Levels descend in order
explanation.text: H1→H2→H3 can express nested sections; skipping a level unnecessarily can make the outline harder to follow, but is not an HTML syntax error by itself.

explanation.title: Machines and people read it
explanation.text: Screen readers can navigate by headings; font size only affects appearance and cannot replace heading structure.

data.boundary: Biggest font size does not mean highest level: heading tags express structure, visual size is styling. Multiple H1s are allowed; the headings should still organize the page clearly.

lessonPractice.title: A page has two H1s. Should one be removed right away?

options.label: Do not judge by the count alone; check that the headings and their levels express a clear outline
options.feedback: Correct. HTML allows multiple H1s; check whether each marks its own main content and whether later headings show their nesting clearly.

options.label: As long as font sizes look right, any tag works
options.feedback: Tags carry structural meaning; font size only changes appearance. Assistive technology can navigate through heading tags.

options.label: Use H1 on whatever text has the largest font size
options.feedback: H1 marks the role of the page's main heading; it is not a style switch for the biggest font.

data.agentPrompt: Review this page's heading structure against its content. Do not treat multiple H1s as an error by themselves; make sure each heading level shows a clear parent-child relationship. Then use an outline view to confirm the structure and tell me which sections each heading introduces.
